```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

The **datarais** package gives access to the microdata of the Brazilian
*Relacao Anual de Informacoes Sociais* (RAIS), the annual formal employment
census of the Ministry of Labour. Files are downloaded from the
[HuggingFace dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/alexsandroprado/rais),
read as a stream and stored in a local DuckDB database that can be queried
with dplyr or SQL.

## Installation

```{r install, eval=FALSE}
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("alexsandroprado/datarais")
```

## Basic workflow

The steps below download real data (files can be large), so they are shown
but not run in this vignette.

```{r workflow, eval=FALSE}
library(datarais)
library(dplyr)

# 1. Check the connection and the available years
rais_status()
rais_available(n = 5)

# 2. Download, parse and load into a DuckDB file
db <- file.path(tempdir(), "rais.duckdb")
rais_load(years = 2022, db_path = db)

# 3. Connect and query with dplyr
con <- rais_connect(db)

rais_tbl(con, year = 2022) |>
  group_by(sigla_uf) |>
  summarise(
    vinculos      = n(),
    salario_medio = mean(vl_remun_media_nom, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  collect()

# 4. Close the connection before exporting to Parquet
DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)
rais_to_parquet(db, output_dir = file.path(tempdir(), "parquet"))
```

`rais_load()` returns a summary of the database, not a connection. Use
`rais_connect()` to query the data, and close the connection with
`DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)` when you are done.

Downloads are stored in a temporary directory and run sequentially by
default. For a persistent cache and parallel downloads, set:

```{r options, eval=FALSE}
options(
  datarais.cache_dir = tools::R_user_dir("datarais", "cache"),
  datarais.workers   = 3
)
```

## A small runnable example

The chunk below uses a tiny table with the same column names as the real
data, so it runs without internet access.

```{r toy}
library(datarais)
library(dplyr)

db  <- tempfile(fileext = ".duckdb")
con <- rais_connect(db, quiet = TRUE)

DBI::dbWriteTable(con, "rais_novo", data.frame(
  ano                = 2022L,
  sigla_uf           = c(23L, 23L, 24L, 35L),
  vl_remun_media_nom = c(1800, 2500, 2100, 4200)
))

rais_tbl(con, year = 2022) |>
  group_by(sigla_uf) |>
  summarise(
    vinculos      = n(),
    salario_medio = mean(vl_remun_media_nom, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  collect() |>
  left_join(uf_codigos, by = c("sigla_uf" = "codigo")) |>
  arrange(sigla)

DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)
unlink(db)
```

In the RAIS tables, `sigla_uf` holds the numeric IBGE code of the state, and
`uf_codigos` translates it to the two-letter abbreviation and the region.

## File layouts

The RAIS file layout changed over time (state files until 2017, region files
from 2018 onwards, and different compression and variables). `rais_layouts()`
summarises the differences.

```{r layouts}
layouts <- rais_layouts(verbose = FALSE)
layouts[, c("periodo", "fonte", "encoding", "compressao")]
```

## Variable dictionary

```{r dictionary, eval=FALSE}
rais_col_dictionary(search = "remun")
rais_col_info("vl_remun_media_nom")
```

## Requirements and troubleshooting

* **7-Zip.** Files up to 2019 use PPMd compression, which needs
  [7-Zip](https://www.7-zip.org/) installed on the computer. Files from 2020
  onwards (LZMA) work without it. `rais_layouts()` shows which periods are
  affected.
* **Disk and memory.** One year of employment records is several GB once
  decompressed. Use a 64-bit R, a few GB of free memory and enough disk for the
  downloads plus the DuckDB file. Start with one or two years.
* **Failed downloads.** Each file is tried three times. A `404` means the file
  does not exist in the repository for that year or region. Check what is
  available with `rais_available()` and `rais_hf_files(years = 2022)`, and
  call `rais_status()` to test the connection to HuggingFace.
* **Slow downloads.** Increase `timeout` (seconds per file), or raise
  `workers` for parallel downloads. The downloads are not repeated: files
  already in the cache are reused.
* **Locked database.** DuckDB allows only one read-write connection to a file at
  a time. Close connections with `DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)`
  before opening the file again or exporting it.
